meaning.text: The 1818 dictionary glosses the word in German as "der Schreyer", the screamer.

appearance.text: It is described as a four-footed animal (Latin "quadrupes").

scene.text: It is a nocturnal animal (Latin "animal nocturnum").
It screams in the night like a goat that is being carried off.

behavior_habitat.text: It screams in the night like a goat that is being carried off.
It is a nocturnal, noisy animal (Latin "animal nocturnum ... clamosum").

rationale.text: All surviving clauses rest on one author, Vuk Karadžić: his 1818 and 1852 dictionaries are counted as one source, and no other source in the entry mentions the creature.
The only people is Serbs, fixed by the context of a Serbian dictionary; neither entry names a people or region.

The entry is a short dictionary gloss of a supposed nocturnal, four-footed, screaming animal, with no tale, belief context or practice recorded. With one 19th-century compiler and no second independent source, it does not meet "regional" (multiple independent sources); it is graded "literary" under the single-compiler rule, although the manifest classes Karadžić as folklore rather than literature, so "cabinet mythology" is not implied.

notes.text: The only sources are two dictionary entries (Karadžić 1818 and 1852). In the 1818 OCR the headword reads "Древавац" and the word before "fortgetragen" (who carries the goat off) is illegible ("оте"), so the clause says only "carried off". The 1852 German gloss is OCR noise; only its Latin ("animal nocturnum, quadrupes, clamosum") and the headword ДРЕКАВАЦ are legible, so the 1852 entry is cited only for those. The native form is given in sentence case; 1852 prints it in capitals.
family: kept as "undead" from the hints file, but neither dictionary entry says anything about the dead; both describe a supposed nocturnal four-footed animal.
peoples_regions: Serbs is fixed by context (a Serbian dictionary); neither entry names a people or region. Bosnians, expected by the hints, are not named by any page opened.
names.variants: no other name found. Searched drekavac, дрекавац, древавац, дрекав, drekav, дрекавца, drekavci across all sources.

origin: neither dictionary entry says where it comes from or who becomes one; no other source mentions it (searched drekavac, дрекавац, древавац, дрекав, drekav, дрекавца, drekavci, screamer, schreyer, clamosum, "animal nocturnum" in all sources).
dealing_with_it: no ward, offering, taboo or escape is given in either dictionary entry; same searches as for origin.
variants: no regional or per-people descriptions; only the two dictionary entries mention it.
related: no page opened links it to another pilot creature.

verify: the grade "literary" reflects a single-author attestation (Karadžić, two editions of one dictionary), not a judgement that the dictionary entry is invented; a second independent folk source would move it to "regional".
